Architecture · engine v0 · for the technical part of the pitch

Every number on the diagram comes from results/RESULTS.md and docs/CLAIMS.md. Slide-ready files are in brand/diagrams/.

How to walk through it in 30 seconds

  1. Open models on the device watch every frame and turn it into features. That's cheap and fast.

  2. Our state tracker keeps a running belief about which step you're on, using the task graph we compiled from the manual. That belief is the core of the product.

  3. Only when something happens (a step ends, it's unsure, or you're stuck) does it ask a rented model one typed question. That's 14% of frames.

  4. We calibrate the answer, feed it back into the belief, and the policy decides whether to say anything at all.

  5. Every session becomes training data, and our local student is already taking over routine checks.

When they ask "isn't this an API wrapper?"
Same model, with and without our layers.

Give the same frontier model the same frames every 5 seconds and it tracks the step 48% of the time. Put our layers around it and it's 54%, at a fifth of the cost.

The API is behind a typed interface.

Swapping Jev, Claude or our own student is a one-line config change. A wrapper can't swap out its only part.

It knows when it doesn't know.

On blurred or blocked views it asked for a better look 77–98% of the time and was never confidently wrong. A stateless model has to answer anyway.

It gets cheaper and better with use.

The flywheel turns sessions into a local student that answers in 0.03 ms for free. The rented model is the teacher, and the student already handles some of its routine checks.

Don't claim
  • That it runs on glasses. The glasses adapter exists but hasn't been tested on hardware. Say it runs live on a camera stream, and glasses are one more input.
  • That these numbers come from maintenance work. They were measured on a public first-person cooking dataset. The procedures transfer; the footage doesn't go on slides.
